summary: Expose private archive history and preserve cached input accounting

delivery.outcome: Expose journal and private archive as explicit read sources with bounded metadata pages and exact day-bound details; preserve known cached-input usage across the OpenAI-compatible proxy and explain it in detail views.
nonGoals: No heuristic historical joins, provider/model policy edits, weakened checks, raw payloads in public metadata, changes to other writers or unreviewed runtime promotion.

architecture.decision: Keep journal selection explicit and make private archive opt-in per read. Metadata-only archive pages carry day/id references and stable timestamp/id cursors; detail lookup uses the exact partition day. Preserve known cached input as OpenAI prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens and render counts without inferring unknown cache as zero.
interfaceChanges: Optional usage source/cursor and detail day selectors.
Add known cached token counts to existing OpenAI usage response.

evidence: Actual shipped JavaScript DOM tests and isolated HTTP/PostgreSQL qualification.

architecture.rollback: Revert this material ticket and restore exact previous runtime source selections. No persistent schema migration or historical row rewrite.

validation.evidence: Private subllm-archive-view-20261027 receipts; exact-head protected CI and independent publication; runtime promotion separate.
